verdict.rationale: Segment's first-party Identity Resolution docs describe an online and offline ID graph that uses cookie IDs, device IDs, emails and custom external IDs. They also say it merges activity from across devices and channels into a single user profile, which covers stitching anonymous and known identifiers. The pack does not document configurable identity-resolution rules (such as identifier priority, merge limits or blocking rules), and nothing independent or hands-on corroborates the claims. Missing for 10: documented configurable resolution rules or settings, explicit description of anonymous-to-known merge behavior, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, anonymous and known activity stitches into one customer profile across devices, with documented and configurable identity-resolution rules

citations.quote: Identity Resolution allows you to understand a user's interaction across web, mobile, server, and third-party partner touch-points in real time, using an online and offline ID graph with support for cookie IDs, device IDs, emails, and custom external IDs.
The Identity Graph merges the complete history of each customer into a single profile, no matter where they interact with your business.
Engage uses [Segment Identity Resolution] to take event data from across devices and channels and intelligently merge it into complete user- or account-level profiles.
